items.title: PULSE Monitor: Black Friday Special
items.summary: Investors are treating U.S. equities like Black Friday specials, seeing the recent pressure on them as their own form of “on sale” event. We discuss our cautionary note that value can be an illusion, as price action typically leads fundamentals. But for now, enjoy the bargain hunting!

items.title: Ferrari: Why Are We Still Rated Neutral?
items.summary: Why do we continue to rate Ferrari Neutral? We note two points: 1) How cheap is RACE at 37x PE for ~10% EPS growth?; and 2) With no unit sales growth and no margin growth, all EBIT/EPS growth is driven by continued ASP expansion, which we're concerned will eventually stop, perhaps in FY28.

items.title: Brazil Equity Strategy: Trabuco Changes the Tone
items.summary: Luiz Carlos Trabuco will be Brazil's next finance minister, ushering in optimism about the prospects for a more market-friendly economic agenda and a potentially stronger commitment to fiscal discipline. But equities' initial rally may not mean a structural change in the economic outlook.

items.title: Venezuela Renace: Revisiting Recoveries Under New Macro Framework
items.summary: The newly published Plan Venezuela Renace identifies $237.5 billion of public-sector liabilities and brings the country's first comprehensive debt framework in years. We offer a recovery framework and explain why our analysis leads us to expect 15%-20% upside across most Venezuelan bonds.

items.title: South Korea's Hawkish Hike Suggests Another Hike in February
items.summary: South Korea raised rates 25 basis points, as expected. We believe Governor Shin remains hawkish about semiconductor-driven strong growth and sticky inflationary pressures through 2027. Our base case is still for a 25-bp hike in February, taking the policy rate to a terminal level of 3.50%.

items.title: Africa Economics & Strategy Weekly: The Uganda Shilling's Selloff
items.summary: Last month's significant selloff in the Uganda shilling has increased uncertainty about the currency's path. Following meetings we attended in Kampala, we offer thoughts about the shilling's outlook and whether the Bank of Uganda needs to make further monetary-policy adjustments.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Thankful for Duration
items.summary: With alarm bells getting louder and continued equity softness, we believe rates should work at this point in the cycle, and the Fed should be the fastest-reacting central bank under sustained market pressure. We offer suggested tactics in this note.

items.title: Our Survey Finds Holiday Spending Looks Strong
items.summary: Our survey in partnership with Citi’s Innovation Lab found plans to spend ~12% more than in the 2025 holiday season. The K-shaped consumer theme showed up in the results, with higher-income households planning to spend significantly more year over year; inflation also remains a big theme.

items.title: The Thesis for EU Autos Just Changed
items.summary: A lack of positive reaction to announced EU auto quotas highlights investors' huge wall of worry, but we think the EU has changed the game, with the thesis for auto makers now significantly different. We see Renault as the obvious beneficiary and add a 90-day positive short-term view.

items.title: U.S. Economics: Strong But Stale Growth and Inflation
items.summary: October's PCE report showed a familiar backdrop of strong growth and sticky inflation. We continue to caution that core PCE in both October and November will be a bit mechanically too strong due to issues stemming from 2025's government shutdown. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Medtronic Shrugs Off Headwinds
items.summary: Medtronic delivered revenue of $9.36 billion, with results muddied by the MiniMed spin-out. We see Buy-rated MDT's business as remaining steadfast: Given guidance was reiterated and strong underlying demand across the portfolio, we remain confident as MDT prepares for upcoming headwinds.

items.title: We're Initiating Coverage of Agility Robotics at Buy/High Risk
items.summary: We launch coverage of Agility Robotics at Buy/High Risk, with an $8 target price. We see AGLT as a unique public-market opportunity to invest in humanoid robots, which we think could represent the next major investment cycle given a potential ~$1 trillion total addressable market by 2032.

items.title: Australia Economics: The Anatomy of Stagflation Risk
items.summary: Australia's October CPI reading reinforced that policymakers remain far from declaring victory on inflation, with the details hawkish. We see little room for a dovish monetary-policy pivot despite labor-market loosening, expecting the cash rate to be on hold until 2027's third quarter.

items.title: Powering America: How Will the Generation Stack Evolve?
items.summary: Given changing assumptions about data-center growth, we take a closer look at how U.S. power supply and demand growth may evolve. We see U.S. power demand accelerating 4.9% through 2040, with meaningful gas additions complemented by nuclear, renewables and other resources.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: Twelve Equity-Strategy Ideas
items.summary: Our Citi China Conference 2026 saw a constructive tone overall, with management teams from leading China and Hong Kong names seeing 2027 as the year in which growth is expected to stabilize or accelerate. In this note we offer a top stock idea from each of our 12 key sectors.

items.title: Have Structural Headwinds Peaked for European Auto Makers?
items.summary: Much of the world has changed, but the EU auto sector has been on the wrong side of these trends and underperformed. What's needed for progress in 2027? Beyond EU policy stances, European auto companies need to be more resilient and better at managing costs, earnings and guidance.

items.title: Sanofi's Deal for Insmed Seems Strategically Sound
items.summary: Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed for $41 billion, a deal that brings marketed and late-stage assets to Sanofi's respiratory portfolio. Although a good strategic fit, and EPS accretive in out years, we note two key reservations about the agreement, which we discuss in detail in this note.

items.title: Sanofi’s Insmed Deal Reinforces Scarcity Value in U.S. Biopharma
items.summary: Sanofi’s proposed deal for Insmed highlights the scarcity value of durable, de-risked growth as key players approach major patent expirations. In this note we consider which names in our coverage have the strongest read-through and which factors are key to that assessment.

items.title: U.S. Banks: Assessing the Implications of a Blue Congress
items.summary: Democrats will control both chambers of Congress in 2027, while President Trump remains in the White House and regulators remain Trump-appointed. We expect extensive hearings and messaging bills, with enacted law limited and selective. We offer further details in this note.

items.title: The Summer's Cruise Strength Has Carried into Fall
items.summary: Our survey of cruise travel agents suggests the positive demand inflection that began this summer has carried into the fourth quarter, with ocean bookings remaining healthy. As we discuss in this note, we are bullish headed into fourth-quarter earnings and 2027 guidance.

items.title: Euro Credit Strategy: 2027 Supply Outlook
items.summary: 2026 credit supply stayed resilient despite macro and micro volatility. EUR IG gross issuance is about €650 billion year to date. For 2027, we expect another year of strong supply with €675 billion gross and €225 billion net in EUR investment grade. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Quantitative Global Macro Strategy: The Quality Factor
items.summary: We recap our case that the classic growth/inflation quadrant framework is incomplete, as levels alone fail to separate regimes cleanly in recessions and also in late-cycle periods, which we may be seeing now. We look at the closest historical analogues to today and offer further analysis.

items.title: NVIDIA Reinstates Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a move we see as removing a key overhang, though uncertainty remains about the investigation into Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence contact and Megaspeed-related export probes. We raise our target price to $240.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: Flows Driving EURUSD Over Fundamentals
items.summary: On Oct. 1 we flagged that EURUSD could reach 1.0850 on misvaluation alone, assuming unchanged relative real yields. Since then, relative real yields are at similar levels and EURUSD is actually now much closer to the 1.0850 area. Historically, such misvaluations tend to be short-lived.

items.title: Global Commodities: Broad-Based Selloff Is a Buying Opportunity
items.summary: Commodity markets' major and broad-based selloff has accelerated, reflecting a broader weakening in risk assets with cyclical equities dropping sharply, alongside a sharp tech equity pullback and a hawkish Fed. That presents a buying opportunity in agricultural commodities, as we discuss.

items.title: What Lies Ahead for Spain?
items.summary: We look at the economic outlook for Spain should elections bring a conservative PP-Vox alliance government to power, as expected. We see GDP overperformance continuing given a housing upswing and a supply-friendly policy mix. We offer further analysis of potential impacts in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Vodafone to Sell
items.summary: We're downgrading Vodafone to Sell. German operations remain under pressure and significant debt consolidation related to the terms of Vodafone's new OXG partnership looms in the medium term. Moreover, despite recent share-price underperformance, we see yet more downside risk.

items.title: Five Big Debates About BT
items.summary: BT remains a divisive stock. Fiber investment is maturing, while the TalkTalk acquisition is modestly accretive. But competition remains tough in UK fixed line, and free-cash-flow consensus forecasts continue to fall. In this note we address five main discussion topics about Sell-rated BT.

items.title: Electrical Equipment Is Now Pricing In a Data-Center Plateau
items.summary: The sell-off in electrical-equipment stocks reflects a confluence of concerns ranging from data-center permitting and financing to export curbs on GPUs. We think data centers plateauing from 2027 is now priced in. We see the sub-sector as oversold, but with few catalysts into year's end.

items.title: U.S. Application Software: Previewing Our 10th Annual Cloud Forum
items.summary: Our 10th annual Cloud Forum will be held at AWS re:Invent on Nov. 30 in Las Vegas. We preview key themes in this note, including shifts in AI diffusion throughout software, harness and multi-model usage, cybersecurity, trends in enterprise tech spending, and more.
